subject: maths
question: Which of the following is the primary reason why copper is widely used as a conductor in electrical wiring?

options.text: Copper has low resistance and high conductivity.
Copper has a low melting point.
Copper has high resistance to electricity.

solution:
The correct answer is __Copper has low resistance and high conductivity**(Option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Copper__ is a widely used conductor in electrical wiring.
 
• Copper has low resistance and high conductivity, making it efficient for electrical applications.
 
• It is durable and can withstand environmental factors, increasing its lifespan in various installations.
 
• Copper's ductility allows it to be drawn into wires without breaking.
 
• It also has a high melting point, which ensures safety in high-temperature conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Aluminum:**

 
 
• It is another commonly used conductor but has higher resistance compared to copper.
 
• Aluminum is lightweight but less durable than copper.
 
 
 
• **Silver:**
 
 
• Silver has higher conductivity than copper but is expensive, making it less practical for general use.
 
• It is used in specialized applications like electronics and spacecraft.
 
 
 
• **Gold:**
 
 
• Gold is an excellent conductor but is very expensive.
 
• It is used in high-precision electronics and connectors.
